details.summary: This is a highly appealing, incredibly practical lunch recipe that perfectly fits the dietary guidelines for fatty liver and type 2 diabetes. To be publication-ready, it requires an added instruction to heat the rice pouch so the grains are actually edible, and the massive sodium overage in the nutrition panel needs to be recognized as a database error and manually corrected.

dimensions.feedback: The combination of sriracha, reduced-sodium soy sauce, and rice vinegar with Greek yogurt perfectly mimics the spicy mayo often found on sushi bowls, bringing creamy heat and bright umami without the excess saturated fat of real mayonnaise.
All ingredients listed are successfully utilized in the instructions without any omissions or unexpected additions.

The instructions tell the reader to divide the ready-to-eat brown rice straight into bowls, but omit heating it. Pre-cooked rice pouches are essentially solid blocks of hard grains that must be microwaved (usually for 90 seconds) to soften before they can be fluffed or eaten pleasantly. Add a step to heat the rice according to package directions before dividing. Additionally, briefly explain how to thaw the shrimp (e.g., 'run under cold water for 5 minutes').
The ingredients and flavor profile effectively capture the desired Asian-American 'sushi bowl' character.
A no-cook, assembly-only method is perfectly suited for a workday lunch bowl built from pre-cooked components.

The computed 1565 mg of sodium per serving is mathematically implausible and almost certainly a database error for the frozen shrimp. 9 oz of standard cooked shrimp (~550 mg total), 2 tsp reduced-sodium soy sauce (~380 mg total), and 2 tsp sriracha (~160 mg total) should yield about 1100 mg of sodium for the entire recipe, or ~550 mg per serving (right on the target ceiling). This is a data discrepancy rather than a recipe flaw, but the printed nutrition panel will need manual correction.
The title and intro accurately and attractively describe the dish without resorting to banned health claims, 'diet' terminology, or hyperbole.
This is a vibrant, easy, and highly appetizing lunch that home cooks will genuinely want to make and eat.

Excellent alignment with the diet's core principles: it features lean protein, a high volume of fresh non-starchy vegetables, healthy monounsaturated fat from the avocado, and a measured whole-grain base.
Carbohydrates (48.9 g) sit perfectly inside the 32–55 g lunch window and arrive via an excellent whole-grain source (brown rice). Added sugar is minimal and purely functional from the sriracha.
Perfectly fits the lunch chapter's goal of quick, desk-friendly meals constructed from simple, everyday components.
This recipe is well under the 30-minute limit. Utilizing pre-cooked shrimp and a ready-to-eat rice pouch makes this a realistic 10-minute preparation.
